label: ai logs for week 15
topic: Added a second login factor (email + SMS code) to the Leave Management System, then gave Manager the same staff accounts table as HR Admin with remove-account and cancel-invitation actions, and fixed forced logout to actually revoke the session and lock the account

content: Opened with a handoff-style recap of the previous session (five UX fixes committed as 5d46ff9; real SMTP email delivery for reset/invite links reviewed twice but uncommitted) and asked to add a second login security feature after username/password: email verification that provides a code, with the same code also sent as a text message to a phone number, working on a live server, and demoable using demo email/phone/code details.

Read the existing login route (routes/user.js), User model, mailer.js, auth middleware and Login.jsx to see what a second factor would slot into. Asked whether the phone-number code should be delivered by a real SMS provider (Twilio — needs a paid account, a purchased number, and setup time) or demo-mode only (no provider, code shown/logged the way the mailer already does in demo mode); the user picked demo mode. Implemented a single 6-digit code delivered by both channels rather than two separate codes: added mfaCodeHash/mfaCodeExpires/mfaAttempts/mfaLastSentAt to the User model and MFA_SENT/MFA_VERIFIED/MFA_FAILED to the SecurityEvent enum; wrote services/smsService.js as an always-demo sender structured so a real provider can be dropped in later without touching callers; added sendMfaCodeEmail to services/mailer.js (real send if Gmail SMTP is configured, else console-logged like the existing reset/invite flow). Split POST /user/login so it stops after the password check and issues a short-lived signed mfaToken (purpose: "mfa", 10 min) instead of an access token, delivering the code via both channels; added POST /user/login/verify-mfa (hashed code, 5 minute expiry, 5-attempt cap, single-use, then issues the real session exactly as login used to) and POST /user/login/resend-mfa (30s cooldown). Fixed services/provisioning.js to actually persist the phone field (it was silently dropped on user creation) and added demo phone numbers to seed.js, including a backfill step for already-seeded accounts. Rebuilt Login.jsx's flow with a "Verify it's you" step: masked email/phone, 6-digit input, resend-with-cooldown, and a demo-mode banner showing the would-be email/SMS codes when no live provider is configured. Verified against a live local MySQL via curl (correct-code success, wrong-code with attempts-remaining, single-use rejection on replay, resend rate-limiting, RBAC on the new routes) and then end-to-end in a real headless-Chromium browser via Playwright — screenshots confirmed the masked-destination banner, the demo codes, the wrong-code error state, and a full successful sign-in reaching the Employee dashboard.
"can u make the unlock accounts in the manager's page also display each staff's details like the one in the hr_admin account, make sure they are sync to each other"

Compared the two existing account tables: HR Admin's page (GET /admin/users, HR_ADMIN-only) showed Name/Role/Country/Team/Annual left/Sick left/Status with Unlock/Force-logout actions, while Manager's page (GET /user/locked, MANAGER + HR_ADMIN) only showed Name/Role/Team/lockedUntil for currently-locked accounts, with its own separately-written query. Rather than just copying columns across, extracted the shared computation into a new services/userDirectory.js (listUsersWithBalances), so both endpoints compute the same annual/sick-remaining figures from the same LeaveBalance rows the same way. Updated GET /user/locked to filter through that helper (still locked-accounts-only at this point) and rewrote Approver.jsx's table to match Admin.jsx's columns and Unlock/Force-logout actions. Verified with curl that /admin/users and /user/locked returned byte-identical fields for the same locked test account, then drove the Manager page in a live browser via Playwright and screenshotted the resulting table to confirm it rendered correctly and that unlocking through it cleared the account from both endpoints afterward.

Repeated the sync request and added three more: give managers and hr_admin a way to remove a staff's account from that same staff-details table; make sure a cancelled invitation stops showing as pending in that table; and make a manager/hr_admin-initiated session revoke or forced logout actually return that user to the login screen and lock their account the same way a failed-login lockout does.

Judged the previous turn's fix insufficient for "sync to each other" — Manager and HR were still two separately-coded routes that merely computed the same numbers, not one shared source of truth — so widened GET /admin/users to allow MANAGER (it already required HR_ADMIN only) and deleted the now-redundant GET /user/locked route entirely, leaving exactly one endpoint both pages call. Extracted a shared frontend/src/components/AccountsTable.jsx used by both Admin.jsx and Approver.jsx, and changed Approver.jsx to show the full staff roster (not just locked accounts) since a manager now needed to see everyone to remove any of them. Added PUT /user/:id/deactivate (MANAGER + HR_ADMIN) as the "remove account" action — a soft delete (status → DEACTIVATED, sessions revoked, login blocked) rather than a hard delete, to preserve leave history and audit records; blocked self-removal so an admin can't lock themselves out mid-session. For cancelled invitations, added a cancelledAt column to UserInvitation and a new POST /invitation/:id/cancel that marks the invite cancelled and deletes the placeholder INVITED user row created up front when the invite was first sent — since that account never really existed as staff, deleting it (rather than deactivating it) is both correct and is specifically what makes it stop appearing as "Invited (pending)" in the accounts table; also blocked resend on a cancelled invite and added a CANCELLED status to the invitations list. For forced logout, found a real pre-existing gap while reading UserSession.js: its own comment claimed revoked tokens were rejected "via authMiddleware," but middlewares/auth.js's validateToken never actually checked session state at all — it only verified the JWT signature, so a force-logout previously did nothing until the token's natural 8-hour expiry. Made validateToken async and check the session's revokedAt on every request. Made PUT /user/:id/force-logout also lock the account for 15 minutes using the exact same fields and thresholds as a 3-strikes failed-login lockout, since revoking sessions alone left the same still-valid password able to log straight back in. Added a lightweight 20-second /user/auth poll in App.jsx so an idle user actually gets bounced to the login screen without needing to click anything first. Verified extensively: curl confirmed a manager can read /admin/users while a plain employee gets 403, that an old token is rejected with 401 immediately after force-logout (not just eventually), that the subsequent login attempt is locked out with the standard lockout message, that self-removal and double-removal are both rejected, and that cancelling an invitation removes it from /admin/users while allowing a clean re-invite of the same email. Then drove it live in a browser: screenshotted Manager's full staff table (with Diana correctly missing her own Remove button), sent and cancelled a real invitation through HR's UI and confirmed the placeholder disappeared from the accounts table, and ran a two-tab Playwright scenario where an idle victim tab — with no reload or interaction — was automatically redirected to the login screen roughly 19 seconds after an HR tab force-logged them out, confirming the background poll works as intended. Restored all test accounts (weiling, priya, somchai) to a clean active/unlocked state afterward.

Please write a handoff summary for this session. Include: what we were working on and the current state, key decisions made and the reasoning behind them, files created or modified, what still needs to be done, and any known issues or things to watch out for.

Wrote a structured handoff summary covering both pieces of work from this session (the second login factor, and the Manager/HR account-management parity work), all implemented and verified live but not yet committed. Covered the key decisions and their reasoning — demo-only SMS by the user's explicit choice, one code sent through two channels rather than two separate codes, an unpersisted JWT (mfaToken) rather than a new table for the pending-login state, making Manager and HR hit the literal same /admin/users endpoint rather than two similarly-shaped ones, soft-deleting removed accounts to preserve history versus hard-deleting cancelled-invite placeholders that never became real staff, and fixing the session-revocation gap in validateToken that had been silently non-functional despite a comment claiming otherwise. Listed every file created and modified. Set out remaining work carried over from before this session (SMTP credentials still not filled in, this session's work still uncommitted, other members' files still not pasted in, the stale-JWT-on-profile-refresh bug still deferred, bulk entitlement still overwriting pro-ration) plus new items from this session (no reactivate path for a DEACTIVATED account, the MySQL root password still sitting in plaintext in committed .claude/settings.json permission entries with a few more entries added this session). Flagged known issues to watch for: the accumulating settings.json permission entries as a place secrets could leak, the changed shape of POST /user/login's response now that MFA is required, the extra DB query validateToken now does per request, and the 20-second poll being a blunt stand-in for real-time push.
